text:
deploy-bot: [ALERT] Canary rollout 2026-03-15 12:05 UTC - runtime-service elevated p99 latency and increased 502s. Severity: P2. See: https://metrics/redwood/runtime/canary

meera: paging oncall - seeing sustained p99 ~2.7s (baseline ~200ms) and 502 spike after the canary push. Canary is ~5% traffic.

oncall: acknowledged, joining. Any initial mitigation?

Samir: I'm looking at the canary hosts now. Kernel fallback logs showing lots of "cuda kernel failure -> falling back to reference" on a subset of nodes. Possible mismatch between new kernel selector and quantized model.

Alex R: hmm that could explain latency & CPU spike. Also seeing batching queue build-up on canary pods - batch size configured higher than expected for short prompts. Queue length up 8x.

meera: customers starting to complain - support thread flagged org: AcmeAnalytics (enterprise) seeing timeouts. We should consider kill-switch for the feature flag or abort rollout.

Samir: agree. Recommending immediate kill-switch flip to route traffic off canary. I can flip the rollout gate now.

Alex R: +1. If we flip, we'll want to confirm fallback behavior routes to stable model variant and that KV cache keys are compatible.

meera: do it. Please post command you run so SRE can audit.

Samir: running:
```
redwoodctl rollout set-state --deployment runtime-service-canary --state disabled --reason "kernel-fallback+batching regression"
kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=runtime-service-canary -o wide
```

Samir: done. Rollout gate disabled at 12:10 UTC. Traffic should start shifting within the next 30s.

deploy-bot: Rollout state change recorded by Samir at 12:10:23 UTC. Canary traffic decreasing from 5% -> 0.5% (propagating).

ops-bot: Autoscaler note: pods on canary are being scaled to zero as they drain. No restarts observed.

Alex R: p99 down to ~210ms on stable after traffic shift. 502s dropping. Good signs.

meera: quick postmortem notes for support: affected window ~12:05-12:10 UTC, roughly 5% of traffic, ~2.3% of global requests experienced >2s latency, top customers impacted: AcmeAnalytics (timeout error spikes), FinSight (elevated tail latency).

oncall: Are we confident this is kernel selector mismatch + batch config? What does the debug log say?

Samir: logs from canary pod:
```
[12:06:11] kernel_selector.cpp: warning: kernel candidate quant8_m_fused not compatible with device compute capability 6.1
[12:06:11] exec_engine.cpp: error: kernel launch failed: cudaErrorLaunchFailure
[12:06:11] runtime_executor.cpp: info: falling back to reference implementation, latency++
[12:06:13] batching.cpp: info: batch size capped at 64 but request mix short prompts -> head-of-line blocking
```

Alex R: that is pretty explicit. The new selector included a quantization-optimized kernel that isn't supported on some cloud GPU SKUs we route to. Combine that with aggressive batching targeting throughput and you get queueing + fallback; fallback path is much slower.

meera: action items: 1) disable rollout (done), 2) create immediate mitigation to restrict kernel selector to supported SKUs, 3) adjust canary batching policy to lighter defaults for mixed prompt lengths, 4) run a controlled canary again with host affinity to compatible GPU SKUs.

Samir: I'm extracting the list of affected SKUs and will push a patch to the kernel selector config. Patch will include a runtime check to skip quantized kernel if device compute capability < 7.0.

Alex R: I'll prepare a short playbook entry for rerouting traffic and steps to abort via `redwoodctl` and `kubectl` incase of reoccurrence.

ops-bot: Noting: incident window closed and mitigated at 12:12 UTC after rollback. Please link any follow-up PRs.

meera: follow-up: open ticket INF-1324 for kernel-selector guard + test matrix to run on all SKUs. INF-1325 for batching default changes. I'll cc product/security for release gating checklist.

oncall: handing off to oncall for next shift to monitor for regressions. oncall, please confirm you're picking this up and will watch the metric dashboard for 3 hours.

oncall: picked up. Will monitor p99, 502s, queue length, and kernel-fallback rate. If any spike, escalate to Samir + Alex.

Alex R: postmortem notes draft incoming. I'll include timeline, root cause (kernel selector + batching policy), impact (2.3% requests high-latency, two enterprise customers with timeouts), and remediation plan.

meera: thanks everyone. Quick wins: add runtime guard, make canary affinity explicit, and add CI matrix to catch kernel incompatibility in model onboarding.

Samir: making the PRs now. tagging @meera @Alex R.

oncall: closing thread for now — monitoring live. :white_check_mark:
